title: TransferTraj: A Vehicle Trajectory Learning Model for Region and Task Trans

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states: 'It achieves an average improvement of 83.70% and 33.68% in zero-shot region transferability,' implying both figures are zero-shot results. However, Section 5.1 clearly states: 'our method achieves improvements of 83.70% and 33.68% over SOTA models in zero-shot and few-shot settings,' indicating 33.68% is actually the few-shot improvement, not zero-shot. The abstract misrepresents the few-shot result as a zero-shot result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 (TP task performance) vs. Table 6 (Ablation study)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 1 reports the full 'TransferTraj' model's Chengdu RMSE as 187.91 ± 8.65 (MAE 144.53 ± 5.25) for the TP task. Table 6 (ablation) reports the full 'TransferTraj' model's TP RMSE as 197.91 (MAE 144.53), which has a different RMSE value for the same model/task/dataset while MAE matches exactly. These two tables report inconsistent RMSE values for the identical full model configuration.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2, Ablation study (SC-MoE discussion) referencing Table 6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims 'our ablation study on SC-MoE demonstrates a substantial performance drop of 14.52% on the OD TTE task.' Using Table 6 values (full model OD TTE RMSE=2.861 vs wo SC-MoE RMSE=3.240; MAE=2.060 vs 2.585; MAPE=9.360 vs 11.584), the computed performance drops are 13.25% (RMSE), 25.49% (MAE), and 23.76% (MAPE) — none of which equal 14.52%, indicating an unsupported/incorrect statistic.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B.2 (Setting) vs. Appendix F (Hyperparameter Study)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix B.2 states: 'The key hyperparameters for TransferTraj are set as L = 2 layers with 128 hidden state dimensions and C = 8 experts in SC-MoE.' However, Appendix F states: 'The optimal value for d is 256; smaller values limit the model's learning capability, while larger values offer minimal performance gains...' This directly contradicts the hidden dimension of 128 used in the main experimental setting.

The text states 'we apply the Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function to the predicted spatial and temporal modalities,' yet the formula given is L_i^t = ||t̂_i − t_i||_2, which is an (unsquared) L2 norm, not a squared error term consistent with MSE. This is inconsistent with the stated loss type (while L_i^s correctly uses squared terms).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2 (Pre-training with the scheme) vs. Appendix B.2 (Setting)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.2 describes masking as selecting a single contiguous sub-trajectory from a randomly chosen start point s to end point e ('we first randomly select the starting point s and ending point e... For each trajectory point in the selected sub-trajectory, ⟨ps,...,pe⟩, complete trajectory point masking is applied'). In contrast, Appendix B.2 describes a different scheme: dividing the trajectory into multiple non-overlapping segments (0.2×|T| segments) and randomly selecting 40% of these segments for point masking, which is a fundamentally different (non-contiguous, multi-segment) masking procedure than the single contiguous-span description in the main text.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix D (Performance Comparison in Task Transfer), Xi'an statistic
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'our model outperforms the state-of-the-art trajectory recovery task baseline by 9.25% and 1.20%' for Xi'an and Porto respectively. Computing the average improvement from Table 9 (MM-STGED vs. TransferTraj w/o ft across the three sparsity levels) yields approximately 9.65%, not 9.25%, while the Porto figure (1.20%) and the μ=16 figures (11.68%, 2.42%) match precisely, suggesting the Xi'an overall figure is miscalculated or inconsistent with the underlying table.

The main text excludes TR from zero-shot region transfer because 'varying road IDs prohibit direct cross-region transfer experiments.' However, Appendix B.4 states that MTrajRec and RNTrajRec were explicitly modified to predict latitude/longitude instead of road segment IDs 'to enable region transferability,' which contradicts the stated rationale that road-ID dependence prevents zero-shot TR transfer for these adapted models.
